expectations.text: The OpenTelemetry packages (hosting extensions, ASP.NET Core instrumentation, OTLP exporter) are added to OrdersApi.csproj
expectations.evidence: The agent ran `dotnet add package` for OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting, OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore, OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http and OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol. Each output line says 'PackageReference ... version 1.20.1 added to file .../OrdersApi.csproj'.

expectations.text: Tracing is enabled via AddOpenTelemetry().WithTracing() with ASP.NET Core instrumentation
expectations.evidence: Program.cs was rewritten with `builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry().ConfigureResource(...).WithTracing(tracing => tracing.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation().AddHttpClientInstrumentation().AddOtlpExporter())`. The build succeeded.

expectations.text: The resource is configured with service name orders-api and version 1.4.0
The OTLP exporter targets http://localhost:4317, preferably from configuration rather than a hard-coded literal
expectations.evidence: The code calls `.AddOtlpExporter()` with no endpoint. It relies on the library default, which happens to be gRPC on localhost:4317. Nothing in Program.cs or appsettings.json sets http://localhost:4317, and appsettings.json was not touched. The endpoint is not explicitly targeted or configured, and the code comment mentions OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT only as an override.
